The notification service sends messages through three channels, email, SMS and push. Each user can choose which channels to enable in their preferences. When an event occurs, the service looks up the user's preferences and sends a message through each enabled channel. Messages are queued, so a temporary outage on one channel does not block the others. Failed messages are retried up to six times, with an increasing delay between attempts. After the final attempt, the message is moved to a dead letter queue for manual review. You can monitor queue depth from the admin dashboard.

The nightly backup job has been failing silently for about a week. I noticed it when I tried to restore a file for a customer and found that the latest backup was from the ninth. The job exits with a success code even when the upload step fails. The root cause seems to be a missing permission on the storage bucket after the policy change last week. I have fixed the permission and run the job manually, and it now completes. But we should also fix the exit code logic and add an alert for missing backups. I will open three separate tickets for those, one for the exit code, one for the alert, and one for the permissions.

This is the entry point for the payment flow, and it is more fragile than it looks. The function first validates the cart, then reserves inventory, then charges the card, then confirms the reservation. If the charge fails, we release the inventory in the finally block, so please do not move that code. The reservation expires after 15 minutes, so slow payment providers will not cause a leak. We tried making this asynchronous last year, and it caused double charges when the user clicked twice. The idempotency key is generated from the cart ID and the user ID, which prevents that. If you add a new payment method, make sure it supports idempotency keys, or it will reintroduce the bug. There are integration tests in the payments folder, and they should pass before you merge anything that touches this file. Talk to the payments team if you have any doubts.
